evidence.claim: Tell Taylor wrote the song on the Blanchard's banks in Findlay in 1908. Publication followed in 1910, when the vaudeville quartet The Orpheus Comedy Four introduced it to audiences.
evidence.quote: The song was written in 1908 while Taylor was sitting on the banks of the Blanchard River in Findlay, Ohio.

evidence.claim: A Kansas City performance sold all 1,000 copies of sheet music Taylor had brought to a Woolworth store. Sales eventually exceeded four million copies, and the song became a barbershop-quartet staple.
evidence.quote: After the group performed the song at a Woolworth store in Kansas City it became so popular that the store sold all 1,000 copies of the sheet music Taylor had brought with him.  Since then over four million copies of its sheet music have been sold and it has become a staple for barbershop quartets.

evidence.claim: Peter Diller placed it at US 224 and Pearl Street in the 1970s, after his father bought it from a bar in Toledo.
evidence.quote: A 16-foot (4.9 m) fiberglass bull statue was placed at the intersection of U.S. Route 224 and Pearl Street by Gilboa then-resident (now mayor) Peter Diller in the 1970s.

evidence.claim: Diller recalled that its height made stoplights difficult to negotiate and that the bull struck the first one on its forehead.
evidence.quote: “Its head was so high that we had to jockey around every stoplight,” recalled Diller. “The first stoplight … we hit it right on its forehead.”

evidence.claim: He said the town wanted something representing the community's strength. The statue became a landmark for travelers passing through Gilboa on US 224.
evidence.quote: “We wanted something that represented the strength of the community,” said Diller, “and what does that more than a big, strong bull?”

evidence.claim: after his father bought it from a bar in Toledo
evidence.quote: When Diller's father was driving in Toledo, Ohio one day, he spotted the bull outside of a bar. He stopped at the bar, and asked if they could sell the bull to him, to which the bar complied.

evidence.claim: The statue became a landmark for travelers passing through Gilboa on US 224.
evidence.quote: The statue has since been a landmark for people passing by Gilboa on U.S. Route 224.

evidence.claim: Findlay's courthouse grew more elaborate as oil and natural gas were discovered in Hancock County. Planned in 1885 to replace a brick courthouse, the new building went up between 1886 and 1888.
evidence.quote: The building, as planned in 1885, was to replace a previous brick courthouse located at the same site. When oil and natural gas were discovered in Hancock County shortly thereafter, the Courthouse was given many of its unique and eclectic stylings.

evidence.claim: A copper John Hancock stands atop the clock tower, with three copper figures below him representing Law, Justice and Mercy.
evidence.quote: The Hancock statue is made of copper and stands next to a pedestal with a law book upon the clock tower.

evidence.claim: A storm blew Hancock off the building in 1922; the statue was repaired the next year. The tower's four clock faces point in the four cardinal directions. Their hand-wound mechanism was electrified in 1925.
evidence.quote: In September 1922, during a severe storm the statue was blown off the courthouse and extensively damaged. It was repaired the following year.

evidence.quote: The clock tower itself has four faces pointing towards each cardinal direction. Each face measures between 8 and 9 feet in diameter. Originally these clocks had a pendulum, 3000 lb bell, and were hand wound until 1925 when they were electrified.
